blocks.text: The Guru accepts the counsel of the Khalsa, has his horse brought, and moves toward the next ground while scouts and survivors keep arriving with fragments of news. (15–17)
The Khalsa then asks openly for permission for martyrdom, requesting leave to stand and die in the Guru's service rather than merely continue retreating. (18)

Standards are raised, drums sound, and the battlefield is marked out so that even before the swords meet, the scene has taken on the structure of chosen sacrifice rather than accidental encounter. (19–23)
